name: PortSense
subtitle: Charger wattage & USB devices
promotional_text: PortSense shows reported charger capacity, battery details, and USB connections in your menu bar. Compare your charger's printed rating and track capacity over time.
description:
PortSense shows reported charger capacity and USB connections in your menu bar. You can also inspect battery charge and condition, including cycle count and raw full charge capacity compared with design capacity, alongside the charger details that macOS exposes for your computer and the hardware connected to it.

Enter the rating printed on your charger to see a warning when the reported capacity is lower. A cable or dock can limit available power, as can a charger shared with another device. Capacity isn't wall power draw.

Open Connections to see the USB names and manufacturers that macOS reports. Link speeds are ceilings, and current values are allocations or limits, so they don't measure throughput or power draw. Missing fields stay unavailable. You can also hide built-in devices from the list when you want to focus on attached hardware.

History keeps up to 60 recent charger readings in memory and clears when you quit. Live polling runs on a 15-second cadence and can wait for an active read, while manual reads and failed attempts can also add entries. A failed read leaves a gap with its time and a retry action.

Sample mode lets you explore the tabs without attached hardware. Hardware readings stay local. There is no account or analytics, and you can read the bundled privacy policy without network access. Launch at Login is optional and off by default.

More Mac menu bar apps by Barframe at barframe.com
review_notes:
Launch PortSense and click the cable menu-bar icon. Click Try Sample to explore all three tabs without hardware, credentials or personal files. The header says Sample. Power shows a 65 W adapter, separate 40.8 W input telemetry, 20 V and 3.25 A, 72% charging battery, signed +18 W, 30.1 °C, estimated 42 minutes to full, 243 cycles and 79% full charge capacity vs design (raw). The ratio differs from the health percentage in System Settings. The sample rating starts at 100 W. set 65 for the matching state, 100 for the warning, or 0 to disable it. Sample rating does not change the live rating.

Connections has ten neutral Sample USB devices; Include built-in devices reveals an eleventh internal hub. A Sample camera advertises USB 3 but reports a USB 2 link ceiling, so it shows a cable advisory. USB values are link ceilings and current allocations or limits, not benchmarks or measured draw. A Sample Thunderbolt dock is listed when viewing the full connection list. History has 20 samples, a 100-to-65 W capacity change and a labelled failed-read gap; test Retry and Clear history. Footer controls remain available while the body scrolls. All three screenshots use Sample data and show different tabs.

Return to Live for actual hardware. Missing fields remain unavailable. Public IOKit reads run on a worker; notifications schedule refreshes and live polling has a 15-second cadence and can wait for an active read; manual reads and failed attempts can add history entries. No hardware is claimed. Entitlement. com.apple.security.app-sandbox; no other entitlements, protected-folder access, helper tools or private APIs. Launch at Login is optional and off by default.

Read privacy opens a bundled policy without network access. Privacy Policy and Support in Settings > About and the footer open bundled policy/support text until the website is configured, then open the configured HTTPS destinations. Command-comma opens Settings. No reviewer credentials, private accounts or accessories are needed for Sample. Real external-device coverage and full VoiceOver navigation remain unknown.
